claim: Tool-MAD assigns heterogeneous external tools (a RAG agent and a live Search-API agent) to separate debating LLM agents rather than a single shared static evidence pool.
stance_target: multi-agent adversarial review architecture for zero-hallucination quality control
scope_conditions: fact verification tasks (FEVER, FEVEROUS, FAVIQ, AVERITEC) and medical QA
quoted_support: we propose Tool-MAD, a multi-agent debate framework that enhances factual verification by assigning each agent a distinct external tool, such as a search API or RAG module.

claim: Tool-MAD outperforms state-of-the-art multi-agent debate frameworks, achieving up to 35.5% accuracy improvement over MAD and 5.5% over MADKE on fact verification benchmarks.
stance_target: effectiveness of adaptive-retrieval multi-agent debate for hallucination reduction
scope_conditions: four fact verification benchmarks (FEVER, FEVEROUS, FAVIQ, AVERITEC), GPT-4o-mini/GPT-4o/Llama-3.3-70B/DeepSeekR1 backbones
quoted_support: Tool-MAD outperforms other multi-agent debate frameworks, achieving up to 35.0% and 5.5% improvements over MAD and MADKE, respectively, with average gains of 18.1% and 3.0%.

claim: Tool-MAD integrates RAGAS faithfulness and answer-relevance scores as real-time, round-level stability signals that gate debate progression, not just post-hoc evaluation metrics.
stance_target: rigid evals / quantitative quality gates for agent outputs during generation, not only after
quoted_support: no prior work integrates metric-guided evaluation into a multi-agent debate structure, nor uses factuality signals to modulate argument selection, judge decisions, or evidence refinement across rounds. Tool-MAD incorporates these signals internally.

claim: Empirically-tuned stability thresholds of faithfulness >= 0.7 and answer relevance >= 0.8 balance precision and debate efficiency, determined from distributional analysis of correct vs incorrect responses.
quoted_support: we adopt 0.7 for faithfulness and 0.8 for answer relevance, which empirically provides stable convergence while maintaining decision quality.

claim: Increasing debate rounds beyond 3 degrades accuracy, showing diminishing and then negative returns from additional agent debate iterations.
stance_target: naive assumption that more agent rounds/iterations always improve quality
quoted_support: Accuracy gradually improves up to round 3 but slightly declines at round 4... excessive debate depth may introduce unnecessary speculation or amplify intermediate reasoning errors.

claim: Heterogeneous tool pairing between debating agents (RAG + Search) outperforms homogeneous tool configurations (RAG+RAG or Search+Search), because diverse evidence sources reduce shared blind spots.
stance_target: diversity of adversarial reviewer tooling improves error detection
scope_conditions: FEVER, FEVEROUS, FAVIQ, AVERITEC ablation study
quoted_support: configurations like RAG+RAG or SEARCH+SEARCH outperformed the VANILLA setup, but still fell short of the hybrid configuration (RAG+SEARCH).

claim: Stability-score-based filtering (faithfulness/answer relevance gating) improves exact-match accuracy across all tested datasets, with up to +4.5% gain on FAVIQ.
stance_target: quantitative rigid evals as control signals (not just post-hoc metrics) improve multi-agent system reliability
quoted_support: scoring feedback consistently improves EM performance across all datasets, with the most significant gain observed on FAVIQ (+4.5%).
